name: TCA9534 8-bit I/O expander
description: Texas Instruments 8-bit I2C/SMBus I/O expander: P0-P7, each a high-impedance input (no internal pull-ups) or a push-pull output (25 mA sink / 10 mA source per pin), plus an open-drain interrupt output. Runs on 1.65-5.5 V with 5 V tolerant I/O. Sold as: SparkFun Qwiic GPIO (DEV-17047; two Qwiic connectors, PTH row GND/3.3V/SDA/SCL plus an INT pad, four 4-pin latch terminals J5: INT/0/1/GND, J8: GND/2/3/3.3V, J1: 3.3V/4/5/GND, J6: GND/6/7/3.3V; I2C and INT pull-ups, ADR0-ADR2 jumpers closed), I2C address 0x27 (0x20-0x27 by cutting ADR jumpers).
eli5: Gives your board 8 extra pins to switch LEDs or read buttons, using only the two I2C wires.

buildNotes: I2C address is 0x20 + (A2 A1 A0). The SparkFun board ships with ADR0-ADR2 jumpers closed (tied to 3.3V), so it answers at 0x27; cut a jumper to clear that bit (2.2k pull-downs).
The TCA9534 has NO internal pull-ups: every input needs an external pull-up (e.g. 10k from the pin to a 3.3V terminal for a button to GND) or pull-down, or it floats.
All pins power up as inputs (Configuration 0x03 = 0xFF) and the Output Port latch 0x01 powers up at 0xFF: write the level first, then clear the Configuration bit, or the pin starts by driving high.
Read pin levels from Input Port 0x00; reading it also clears INT. Reading Output Port 0x01 gives the latch, not the pin.
Each pin sinks up to 25 mA but sources only 10 mA; chip total 200 mA through GND and 80 mA through VCC: always put a resistor in series with an LED.
The board's SDA/SCL/INT pull-ups go to its 3.3V rail: power it from 3.3 V (Qwiic) with an ESP32 or Pico.
Connectors sit on several edges (PTH row, INT pad, four latch terminals), so Sparkbench wires it with jumper leads.

driver.code:
# TCA9534 8-bit I2C I/O expander (TI SCPS197D), MicroPython driver.
# Register map (command byte, datasheet Table 3):
#   0x00  Input Port          read-only, the levels on the pins (inputs and outputs)
#   0x01  Output Port         output latches (power-up 0xFF); reads back the latch
#   0x02  Polarity Inversion  1 = invert that input (power-up 0x00)
#   0x03  Configuration       1 = input (power-up 0xFF), 0 = push-pull output
# Address 0x20 + A2A1A0 (0x20-0x27). The SparkFun Qwiic GPIO ties A0-A2 high
# through closed jumpers, so it answers at 0x27 out of the box.
# The TCA9534 has NO internal pull-ups (unlike the TCA9554): an input pin
# left unconnected floats. Give every input an external pull-up or pull-down.

_INPUT = 0x00
_OUTPUT = 0x01
_POLARITY = 0x02
_CONFIG = 0x03

INPUT = 1
OUTPUT = 0


class TCA9534:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x27):
        """addr = 0x20 + A2A1A0 (0x27 on the SparkFun board with all ADR jumpers closed)."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val & 0xFF]))

    def _r(self, reg):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 1)[0]

    def _bit(self, reg, pin, on):
        if not 0 <= pin <= 7:
            raise ValueError('pin must be 0-7')
        v = self._r(reg)
        v = v | (1 << pin) if on else v & ~(1 << pin)
        self._w(reg, v)

    def pin_mode(self, pin, mode):
        """mode INPUT or OUTPUT. Set the output level with value() first:
        the latch powers up at 1, so a pin made an output drives high."""
        self._bit(_CONFIG, pin, mode == INPUT)

    def invert(self, pin, on=True):
        """Polarity inversion of an input pin (Input Port reads the opposite level)."""
        self._bit(_POLARITY, pin, on)

    def value(self, pin, val=None):
        """Read a pin's level (Input Port), or set its output latch (Output Port)."""
        if val is None:
            if not 0 <= pin <= 7:
                raise ValueError('pin must be 0-7')
            return (self._r(_INPUT) >> pin) & 1
        self._bit(_OUTPUT, pin, val)

    def read_port(self):
        """All 8 pin levels, bit n = Pn."""
        return self._r(_INPUT)

    def write_port(self, val):
        """Set all 8 output latches, bit n = Pn."""
        self._w(_OUTPUT, val)

    def config_port(self, inputs):
        """8-bit direction mask in one go (1 = input, 0 = output)."""
        self._w(_CONFIG, inputs)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from tca9534 import TCA9534, INPUT, OUTPUT

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
io = TCA9534(i2c)          # address 0x27 (ADR0-ADR2 jumpers closed on the board)
io.value(0, 0)             # latch P0 low first (it powers up at 1)...
io.pin_mode(0, OUTPUT)     # ...then make P0 an output for an LED (through a resistor)
io.pin_mode(4, INPUT)      # P4 reads a button to GND (add a 10k pull-up to 3.3V)
while True:
    pressed = 1 if io.value(4) == 0 else 0
    io.value(0, pressed)   # LED on while the button is held
    print('BTN=%d LED=%d' % (pressed, pressed))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
